purpose: Progesterone is a natural hormone used to help balance estrogen in women who still have a uterus and are going through menopause. It is also used to support pregnancy in women having fertility treatments, and to help restart periods in women who have stopped having them for unexplained reasons.
how_it_works: Progesterone is the same hormone your body naturally makes, especially during the second half of your menstrual cycle and during pregnancy. It works by preparing and protecting the lining of your uterus, keeping it healthy and preventing it from becoming too thick. Think of it as a signal to your body that helps regulate your monthly cycle and supports a healthy pregnancy environment.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or dizziness (especially with the oral capsule, so it is best taken at bedtime), headache, bloating, breast tenderness, mood changes, nausea, and vaginal discharge or irritation if using the vaginal form.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have ever had blood clots, stroke, liver disease, breast cancer, or an allergy to peanuts (the capsule contains peanut oil). Do not use if you are pregnant unless specifically directed by your doctor for fertility support. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery after taking the oral capsule since it can make you very sleepy. Call your doctor right away if you notice sudden chest pain, vision changes, severe headache, or leg swelling.
typical_dosing: The dose depends on why you are taking it. For hormone therapy, a common dose is 200 mg by mouth once a day at bedtime for 12 days each month. For fertility support, vaginal suppositories or gel are used once or twice daily as directed by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions since doses vary quite a bit depending on your situation.
